ios.desc:
You already have a great todo app and calendar on your phone; they're called Reminders and Calendar. The problem is, they don't talk to each other about your free time!

Reminder Wrangler fixes that. It takes the todos in your Reminders app and schedules them into free slots on your Calendar — automatically, in the background. When a todo conflicts with a meeting, it moves. When you don't get to something, it reschedules to the next day. You never have to open Reminder Wrangler to make this work. Just keep using Calendar and Reminders the way you already do.

WHY THIS MATTERS

A todo list without a time slot is just a list of things you feel bad about not doing. When your todos show up on your calendar between meetings, they become real plans. You can see what's realistic for today and what isn't. That's the difference between "I have 20 things to do" and "I have three things to do before lunch, and time to do them."

BUILT FOR HOW YOUR BRAIN ACTUALLY WORKS

If you have ADHD — or if you've just noticed that trying out five productivity apps doesn't actually make you more productive — Reminder Wrangler was made for you. It doesn't replace anything. It doesn't ask you to learn a new interface or change your workflow. It works entirely through the Calendar and Reminders apps you already know. One less app to get distracted by.

HOW IT WORKS
• Create reminders in the Reminders app like you normally would — no need to pick a time
• Reminder Wrangler finds free slots on your calendar and schedules your todos there
• If a todo conflicts with a meeting or another reminder, it gets moved automatically
• If you don't complete a todo, it reschedules to your next available free time
• Runs in the background — no daily check-ins required

Reminder Wrangler is a quiet utility that does one thing well: it keeps your todos close to now, on the calendar you're already checking.

quotes.text:
Yeah! I mean I published it on the app store, too. It does three core things:
1) Makes sure every reminder gets a date and time if it doesn't have one
2) Snowplows them ahead of you, so if you go on vacation they're still in the near future
3) Moves reminders out of the way if you accept or create a calendar event conflicting with it

It also preserves ordering when moving things (hence my snowplow approach).

Soon it'll summarize what you did that day so you can feel good about what you get done - that's coming shortly, I'm testing the feature for another few days.

There are a bunch of settings to tweak this - picking what reminder lists to include, setting a time window for when it'll reschedule things, etc.

This should link to it:

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/reminder-wrangler/id6759400510
